Context:
**Project overview of Auto Task via Google Meeting (Salesforce DX), with risks found**

This was a read-only review of the whole project. No code was changed. The app connects each user to Google, and a scheduled job then works through each active Meeting_Configuration__c in turn. For each one it pulls the Gemini meeting notes from Google Drive (Google Docs whose names start with '<Config Name> -'), reads the 'Suggested next steps' section and creates Meeting_Task__c records with status 'Pending Reviewed'. When a task is approved, a record-triggered flow creates a standard Task. The review found a deployment blocker and a silent-failure bug, listed under open issues.

**Open issues**
- MeetingTaskBatch calls MeetingTaskHelper.getAssigneeIdByNameMatch, but no MeetingTaskHelper class exists in force-app. Deploying from this repo will fail unless the class already exists in the target org. Get it from the org or write it.
- If GoogleAuth.getValidAccessToken() returns a blank token, MeetingNotesQueueable.execute returns without calling moveToNext(). The job chain stops, so every configuration after the failing one is skipped for that run. That return also comes before `insert logs`, so the 'Authentication token is blank.' Meeting_Log__c is never saved and the failure leaves no record.
- Tokens come from the running user's User record (GoogleAuth.getValidAccessToken). The scheduled job therefore uses the Google account of whoever scheduled it, not the account of each configuration's owner.
- objects/User/ has about 90 field files from managed packages (Pardot, Maps, SBQQ, et4ae5 and others). Only the four Google_* fields belong to this project. Deploying the whole folder may conflict with those packages, so consider trimming it.
- There are no Apex test classes or LWC Jest tests in the repo, so the code can't reach the test coverage Salesforce requires to deploy to production.
- Video_Meeting__c appears to be an older data model that the main notes-to-tasks process doesn't use. It is a candidate for removal once that is confirmed.
- The project folder is not a git repository yet.

**Enterprise-readiness assessment of Auto Task via Google Meeting, which found a token leak to the browser**

The user asked whether the project is ready for enterprise use. The verdict was no: it is a single-org proof of concept. Rechecking the code found a new critical security issue: every connected user's Google access token is sent to the browser. It also confirmed that tokens and the OAuth client secret are stored in plain text. No code was changed. Claude offered to fix the token leak, and the user has not replied yet.

**Open issues**
- CRITICAL: the user-filter method in GoogleGeminiService (about line 105) runs SELECT Id, Name, Google_Access_Token__c FROM User and returns those User records through an @AuraEnabled UserFilterWrapper.users. Any user who can open the LWC can read every connected colleague's live Google token in browser dev tools, and that token can read their Drive. Fix: remove the token from the query (use the token only for a server-side filter, or a separate IsNotBlank check) or return a DTO with only Id and Name. Fix this before any further rollout.
- The Google_Access_Token__c and Google_Refresh_Token__c fields on User are unencrypted LongTextArea fields. Meeting_PS gives read and edit access to both, and Video_Meeting_PS also grants permissions on them, so admins and permission-set holders can see the tokens.
- The Google_Token__mdt object, which holds Client_Secret__c (a plain Text field), has Public visibility, so the OAuth client secret is not protected. This adds to the case for the proposed (not yet agreed) move to an External Credential with per-user principals plus a Named Credential.
- Other enterprise gaps: an AppExchange security review is needed if the app will be sold; the Drive-wide OAuth scope usually needs approval from the customer's Google Workspace admin; and token revocation, callout limits and scaling to many configurations are not handled.

**Build vs buy: is there an off-the-shelf alternative to Auto Task via Google Meeting?**

The user asked whether a standard extension already does what this app does. Web research found nothing that reads Gemini's 'Take notes for me' Docs and creates Salesforce Tasks with a review step, so the custom app still fills a real gap. Products that overlap are Salesforce Einstein Conversation Insights (ECI) and third-party AI note-takers. No code was changed and no build-vs-buy decision was made. The user has not confirmed whether 'extension' meant a VS Code extension or something else.

**Open issues**
- Not yet decided whether to keep the custom app or switch. The open issues from earlier handoffs (the token leak in GoogleGeminiService, the missing MeetingTaskHelper, no tests) count toward that choice.
- ECI is the closest Salesforce-native option, and a third-party guide lists Google Meet as a native integration. But it needs a separate paid Sales Cloud Einstein add-on, it works from recorded meetings rather than Gemini notes Docs, and nothing found shows it creating Task records with a review/approve step like this app's 'Pending Reviewed' flow. Check this in a trial before relying on it.
- Einstein Activity Capture and the Salesforce Gmail/Chrome extension only sync emails and calendar events. They do not turn meeting notes into tasks, so they are not alternatives.
- Third-party tools (tl;dv, Gong, Avoma, Fireflies, Fathom) push action items to Salesforce but use their own recorder bot instead of Gemini and are priced per user, so adopting one replaces the Gemini workflow rather than extending it.

The user then asked what publishing the app as a product would cost. If the product uses one shared Google OAuth client, it needs Google verification (about 4-12 weeks) and a yearly third-party CASA assessment (about $540-$1,000 for self-serve Tier 2; some labs charge $3k+).

**Wrote the missing MeetingTaskHelper class and the first Apex test classes for Auto Task via Google Meeting**

All 5 objects (4 custom objects plus Google_Token__mdt) were already in the repo, so no objects were created. The real deploy blocker was the missing MeetingTaskHelper class. Claude wrote that class from scratch and added test classes for every Apex class, plus a shared HttpCalloutMock (GoogleHttpCalloutMock). None of this has been compiled, deployed or run against any org. The next step is a check-only validation: sf project deploy validate --source-dir force-app --target-org kapil_GoogleOrg --test-level RunLocalTests.

**Decisions**
- MeetingTaskHelper.getAssigneeIdByNameMatch matches the user's first name only, because MeetingTaskBatch queries only FirstName. Meeting attendees are checked first; if several are named, the one mentioned earliest wins, since Gemini puts the owner first (e.g. '[Name] do X'). If no attendee matches, it falls back to all active users, but only accepts a first name exactly one active user has. Matches are whole-word and ignore case ('Ann' does not match 'Annual'). If nothing matches safely it returns null and the task is created unassigned rather than given to the wrong person.
- Tests create no users and run as the current user, changing only the Google_* fields on that user. Reason: managed-package (FSSK) validation rules on User could block inserting test users.
- The GoogleAuth tests read the real Google_Token__mdt record, because Apex tests cannot create custom metadata records.
- The queueable tests call MeetingNotesQueueable.execute(null) directly instead of enqueueing it. Test.setCreatedDate fixes the order of configurations, so each chain is only one level deep. This avoids Salesforce's ban on chaining queueable jobs in tests.
- Tests do not assert on Meeting_Log__c rows from the queueable's early-return paths (see open issues), so the tests do not treat that bug as correct behaviour.

**Open issues**
- Nothing is compiled or run yet. Run the check-only validation, and first confirm the kapil_GoogleOrg alias is the intended org (a second org, 00Dg5000005rrsvEAA, is in the local CLI cache).
- MeetingTaskHelper was written from scratch. If a version already exists in the org, deploying will overwrite it. Retrieve it first (sf project retrieve start -m ApexClass:MeetingTaskHelper) and compare.
- Bug, wider than the earlier handoff recorded: MeetingNotesQueueable returns before `insert logs` in four cases (start date blank, past end date, blank token, and a Drive error that returns no notes), so those Meeting_Log__c records are never saved. Suggested fix: move `insert logs` into a finally block. Not fixed yet.
- The GoogleAuth and GoogleOAuthCallbackController tests need the Google_Token__mdt record deployed with a non-null Client_Id__c and Client_Secret__c, or they fail.
- GoogleGeminiServiceTest approves a task, which triggers the real Meeting_Task_After_Save_Flow (it creates a standard Task owned by the assignee). If that flow is broken in the org, this test fails.
- Assignee matching uses first names only, so users with the same first name, or steps that don't name anyone, produce unassigned tasks. Matching on full names would need MeetingTaskBatch to query LastName/Name too.
